reason: E2 directly supports that uniformly distributed TiC increases creep strength, recrystallization temperature, and grain boundary strengthening, but it does not provide evidence for improved ductility, delayed crack initiation, or enhanced toughness, which are key premises of the proposed mechanism. E1 only supports the processing route, not the mechanical behavior claims.
premises: Uniformly distributed TiC precipitates form in W-based alloys via Ti addition and SPS
TiC precipitates pin grain boundaries and impede dislocation motion
TiC dispersion raises recrystallization temperature and creep strength
Suppressed strain localization delays crack initiation and improves toughness
These mechanisms operate under fusion-relevant high-temperature conditions
